title: Game Tree
body_html:
Game Tree

The tree of a finite perfect-information extensive game is a finite connected directed acyclic graph with a distinguished origin $\theta$. Every non-origin node has a unique predecessor, and iterating predecessors eventually reaches $\theta$.

Terminal nodes are those with no successors. Decision positions are nonterminal nodes. Each decision position has a nonempty successor set.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 6.2.1] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Tree of nodes, origin, predecessor map, terminal nodes, and successors.

lean_refs.name: GameTree
lean_refs.signature:
inductive GameTree (N : Type*) (U : Type*) : Type _
  | Leaf (payoff : N → U) : GameTree N U
  | Node (mover : N) (head : GameTree N U) (tail : List (GameTree N U)) :
      GameTree N U
namespace GameTree
variable {N U : Type*}
/-- The full child list at a `Node`, as a guaranteed non-empty list. -/
@[simp]

lean_refs.name: GameTree.children
lean_refs.signature:
def children : GameTree N U → List (GameTree N U)
  | Leaf _ => []
  | Node _ h t => h :: t
/-- Children of a `Node` are never empty. -/

lean_refs.name: GameTree.size
lean_refs.signature:
def size : GameTree N U → ℕ
  | Leaf _ => 1
  | Node _ h t => 1 + h.size + (t.map size).sum
/-- Size is always positive. -/
lean_refs.docstring: Structural size, used for well-founded recursion.
